contract.name: seam-contract
contract.supersedes: seam-contract/1 (implicit, never frozen as a document)
contract.amendment_rule: Amendments are recorded as decisions with the contract version bumped and the digest recomputed. U6 judges against a specific contract SHA.

contract_gaps_at_phase_a: C1 gap: no configurable termination_reserve_seconds (deadline hard-derived time.time()+cap, kanban_review_state.py:169)
C2 gap: no verified process-group identity (group exists via start_new_session but never verified/recorded/enumerated)
C3 gap: no native cohort export with generation/watermark/completeness fields or finalized-through fence
C4 gap: review_actions.deadline is wall-clock, not boot-scoped monotonic with half-open not_before/expires_at
C5 gap: no armed->released command-release token; arming and release are the same dispatcher tick

capabilities.title: Configurable termination reserve
capabilities.plan_v2_basis: plan v2:147 (launcher subtracts reserve from both enforcement boundaries), 472 (config source, two-stage validation), 474 (insufficient_safe_window)

caller.who: the gated launcher (C5) and the supervisor; the config loader at kanban.review_feedback is the single source. Harness-side read lives in hermes-config Phase B slices, not the candidate.
caller.module_surface: kanban_review_state.py config path; launcher/supervisor deadline construction

preconditions: (a) at config load — `termination_reserve_seconds` is a finite positive integer, and smaller than every issuable lease/cap duration
capabilities.atomic_persistence: the effective reserve value is recorded per action in the lease/receipt row in the same claim transaction that issues the lease. Config changes apply only to actions reserved after the change — never retroactively; receipts keep the value each action actually used.
capabilities.idempotency: re-reading config does not rewrite recorded reserves; an action's recorded reserve is immutable once issued.
capabilities.readback: the per-action recorded reserve is visible in the lease/receipt row via the supported export; the harness reads the effective value, never the config default.

capabilities.title: Verified process-group containment
capabilities.plan_v2_basis: plan v2:200 (mandatory proof cases), plan v2:23 (setsid residual accepted, detected and recorded, never claimed prevented)

caller.who: the supervisor/dispatcher supervision path only. start_new_session=True is kept - it is deliberate and already gives the launcher/worker a private session and process group.
caller.module_surface: kanban_db_dispatch.py spawn path; supervisor in kanban_review_state.py

preconditions: the spawned launcher/worker pgid is verified to match the recorded pid and its start identity before any signal may be sent to the group
killpg invariants hold fail-closed — never signal pgid <= 1, never signal the supervisor's own group, never signal a group whose recorded (pid, start identity) no longer matches the live check.
capabilities.atomic_persistence: pgid + leader start identity persist in the `armed` transaction (with C5), not at spawn time alone.
capabilities.idempotency: survivor enumeration is a read; repeated scans are idempotent. Re-verification at signal time is mandatory, not cached.
capabilities.readback: recorded group identity and survivor lists are visible in the receipt/watchdog row via the supported export.

capabilities.title: Cohort generation/watermark export and finalization fence
capabilities.plan_v2_basis: plan v2:182 (watermark = authorization sequence; finalization fence), plan v2:86 (board identity anchor), plan v2:202 (native atomic admission fence; four race cases)

caller.who: the managed-claim transaction allocates the authorization sequence; a single native finalization op is the only fence writer; the read-only export is available to the config harness/validator.

preconditions: export ordering is fixed and tested: sequence allocation -> claim commit -> export snapshot (one complete read of committed state) -> finalization (fixes `finalized_through` and `exhausted_at`) -> receipt eligibility.
capabilities.atomic_persistence: finalization is ONE transaction: disables further cohort claims, includes every committed claim through the watermark, fixes the complete generation and `exhausted_at`, marks receipt eligibility pending/settled. Isolation: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / single-writer semantics on the board DB; claim-vs-fence tests run across separate OS processes, not threads.
capabilities.generation_watermark: native cohort exports carry: board identity (`workflow_board.board_id` paired with canonical DB path + filesystem device recorded at creation), authorization sequence (allocated in the managed-claim transaction), export generation, `finalized_through` watermark, completeness flag. An earlier-starting sibling committed before the fence but closed late keeps finalization pending (plan v2:182).
capabilities.idempotency: repeating a finalization for the same generation returns the same finalized record; a post-fence claim fails the fence. A copied DB at a different canonical path/device is rejected; a legitimately restored board re-identifies only via a new operator decision record naming the restore (same authority class as enrollment); otherwise path/device mismatch holds.
capabilities.readback: the cohort export is the supported read-only path carrying identity + generation + watermark + completeness; `show --json` disagreement can only place the projection in `reconciliation_required`, never alter native state.

capabilities.title: Boot-scoped monotonic lease bounds
capabilities.plan_v2_basis: plan v2:145 (one boot-scoped monotonic domain; cross-boot comparisons illegal), plan v2:147 (boundary rules), plan v2:213 (timeout = min of command cap, lease remaining, allowance remaining)

caller.who: the launcher (deadline construction and every comparison) and the supervisor (enforcement boundaries); every deadline comparison in the review seam is replumbed to this domain.

preconditions: lease `not_before`/`expires_at`, command start/finish, and `exhausted_at` all persist in one boot-scoped monotonic domain
wall time is audit/correlation only. Clock choice (frozen): `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` via `time.clock_gettime(time.CLOCK_BOOTTIME)` — monotonic-including-suspend
Python's `time.monotonic()` excludes suspend on Linux and would undercharge a suspended host. Boot identity source: `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`.
capabilities.atomic_persistence: lease bounds persist in the claim transaction (with C5's `claimed_unarmed` persistence); command start/finish endpoints persist at observation.
capabilities.generation_watermark: `exhausted_at` participates in the C3 finalization fence.
capabilities.idempotency: replayed endpoints are idempotent; a previously trusted open prefix is never lowered by a later earlier endpoint — high-water retained, discrepancy recorded, hold for reconciliation.
capabilities.readback: lease bounds and endpoints read back in the monotonic domain via the lease row/export; wall timestamps ride along as audit only. Legacy `deadline` values are read as wall history and never reinterpreted as monotonic bounds (migration, plan v3).

capabilities.title: Armed/released command-release token state machine
capabilities.plan_v2_basis: plan v2:82 (durable fail-closed state machine; recovery rules), plan v2:84 (projection failure before/after release), plan v2:200 (verify/record/arm before release), plan v3 gated-launcher section (release mechanism, frozen here by reference)

caller.who: the dispatcher managed-claim path is the only actor that advances states; the gated launcher is the only executor.
caller.module_surface: kanban_review_state.py action states; kanban_db_dispatch.py spawn path (gated launcher)

preconditions: only the original verified `released` state may execute
the command-release token is persisted separately from the run claim

enrollment is an explicit durable predicate (`enrolled` marker persisted at reservation, default absent/false for legacy rows), so "non-managed claim paths rejected for enrolled tasks" has a defined key.
capabilities.atomic_persistence: the `armed` transaction persists verified group identity + watchdog record + state; token issuance is separate and follows projection verification.
capabilities.generation_watermark: n/a directly; the action participates in the C3 cohort watermark.
capabilities.idempotency: token replay is idempotent (a second delivery of the same token does not re-launch or re-arm).
capabilities.readback: action state, token-present flag (not the token), armed group identity, and watchdog record are visible via the supported export; the token itself is never part of any export.
